page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 45 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of the n1-highcpu-4 in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield scores of 1125.48 and 2941.66 respectively, both categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench testing reports a single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1979.0, reflecting modest overall processing speeds. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show limited throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression at 18.99 GB/sec and passmark CPU encryption at 1338.88.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-4 is its highly constrained memory capacity of 4.0 GB alongside 4 vCPUs, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints or high-speed local storage. Given its performance profile, it is suited for lightweight compute workloads, basic static web serving, simple software compilation, and minor text processing tasks.
